questions.q: An owner asks: 'What exactly is the Brain?' Which one-liner is correct?
options: A per-business memory of owner-approved facts
A standalone chatbot that lives on the salon's website
An industry-wide knowledge base every Zoca business contributes to
An auto-trained model unique to each staff member's login
questions.explain: The Brain is a per-business memory layer of owner-approved facts that serves every Zoca AI. It's not shared across businesses, not a chatbot, and not per-user.

questions.q: A skeptical owner asks: 'If I correct one fact, why does it take effect everywhere?' Which explanation is correct?
options: Each Zoca AI keeps a local copy that syncs nightly

questions.explain: Every Zoca AI reads live from the same Brain ‚Äî no syncing or per-tool pushes. That's why one correction shows up everywhere immediately.

options: A Brain belongs to one business ‚Äî never pooled
Only pricing facts are shared; everything else is per-location
Yes, all facts are shared across every location in the chain
Facts get pooled across all Zoca businesses for benchmarking
questions.explain: Per-business ownership is a foundation principle: a Brain belongs to one business, never pooled or shared. Multi-location handling lives in product settings, not the Brain.

questions.q: A spa owner says: 'I want this fact used on calls but NOT in my blog.' What's the honest answer?
options: Yes, per-surface control is fully available today
Yes, but only on pricing facts in the Brain
We can do that for staff accounts only
Not yet ‚Äî a confirmed fact reaches every tool
questions.explain: Per-surface control is a known gap. Once a fact is confirmed, every Zoca AI can use it. Don't promise per-tool gating.

questions.q: An owner asks what happens if a wrong fact ends up in the Brain. What's the most honest framing?
options: The Brain auto-detects and removes contradictions before they ship
It'll repeat across every Zoca AI until corrected
Wrong facts only affect the surface they came from

questions.explain: Caveat: a wrong fact in the Brain will be relayed by every grounded AI. That's why owner-approved confirmation matters ‚Äî and why corrections are also one-touch.

options: Canvas
Validate
Preview

options: Card only ‚Äî PayPal and Apple Pay not supported
PayPal or Apple Pay only ‚Äî credit card not supported
Card, PayPal, and Apple Pay all supported equally
Bank transfer or credit card, but no digital wallets
questions.explain: Trial requires a valid, funded card. PayPal and Apple Pay are not supported today ‚Äî don't promise them.

questions.q: A 3-month customer adds the Loyalty Agent. Does she need to sign a new contract?
options: Yes ‚Äî a brand-new contract and a new card on file
No ‚Äî contract augments automatically, no re-signing, same card
Yes ‚Äî the trial restarts from day one when adding agents
She has to book an offboarding call before adding the agent
questions.explain: There's one contract per business. Adding agents later augments it automatically ‚Äî no re-signing, same card on file, joined to the same subscription and cycle.

questions.q: A trialing customer wants to cancel on day 5. What's the right path?
options: Email a written cancellation request to support today
Let the card expire on its own at month end
Click a single cancel button in the account settings page
Book an offboarding call, not a one-click toggle
questions.explain: Cancellation isn't one click ‚Äî it requires booking an offboarding call so there's a human conversation first. That's deliberate retention design, not a dark pattern.

questions.q: An owner asks where her card details actually live. What's accurate?
options: On the owner's local device in the iOS keychain
On Zoca's own servers in an encrypted vault
On the salon's current booking platform's database
With Zoca's billing provider, not Zoca directly
questions.explain: Card details sit with Zoca's billing provider (the payment processor), never on Zoca's servers directly ‚Äî the standard PCI-safe pattern.

questions.q: An AE is scoping onboarding. How many platform journeys are there, and what decides which one a prospect lands in?
options: Three journeys, decided by the plan tier they bought
Five journeys, decided by their current booking platform
Five journeys, decided by how much the customer pays
Three journeys, decided by the customer's location and state
questions.explain: There are five platform journeys; the prospect's current booking platform is what selects the journey ‚Äî not their plan or price.

questions.q: A prospect asks 'will Zoca change anything in my Booksy?' On the secure-automated-assistant journey, what's accurate?
options: Signs in read-only, never modifies the existing system
Edits and updates appointments in the salon's existing system
Deletes the old booking platform after migrating the data
Charges the salon a one-time connection fee at setup
questions.explain: The secure automated assistant is read-only ‚Äî it logs in to pull data but never modifies the existing system. That's how it can connect to platforms without official APIs.

questions.q: A prospect asks 'is the migration journey more expensive than the direct one?' What's the right answer?
options: The flagship migration journey costs the most of all five each month
Direct connection is the cheapest of all five journeys
No price difference ‚Äî journey changes setup, not the bill
The secure automated assistant adds a small monthly surcharge
questions.explain: Pricing is identical across journeys. The journey changes how setup happens, not what the customer pays.

questions.q: On the flagship migration journey, what actually happens to the salon's setup?
options: She stays entirely on her old booking platform forever
Data is read read-only without ever being moved over
Two systems are connected but no data is actually moved
She moves fully onto Zoca's bookings and payments
questions.explain: The flagship migration is a full move onto Zoca Bookings & Payments ‚Äî the end-state where Zoca owns the booking+payment rail end-to-end.

questions.q: An AE is unsure which environment to onboard a new customer in. What's the rule?
options: Always use production ‚Äî it's the most up-to-date environment
Let the prospect choose which environment to onboard in
Confirm environment first ‚Äî newest build lives in demo/sandbox
Use whichever environment loads faster on the customer's device
questions.explain: The newest build lives in the demo/sandbox environment first; production can lag by days or weeks. Always confirm the current environment with the team before a live setup.

questions.q: A prospect asks 'so what's onboarding like, in one line?' Which pitch is correct?
options: 'Sign up online and explore on your own'
'Three steps, one screen-share, you're live'
'Pay first, then we set everything up'
'Download our app and we'll call you'
questions.explain: The one-liner from the onboarding doc: three steps (platform setup, agent setup, formalities), one screen-share, and you're live.

questions.q: Roughly how long does it take to go from screen-share start to a live website + bookings + AI receptionist for a typical single-location shop?
options: A full working day
Well under an hour
About three business days
Around two to three hours
questions.explain: Well under an hour for a single-location shop with a laptop or iPad on hand. The whole flow is engineered for one assisted session.

questions.q: During Front Desk setup specifically, what does the prospect actually do on the call?
options: Sign the service contract and add a payment card to the account
Connect platform, set up number, pick voice, set forwarding, test call
Only confirm services and prices, nothing else on the call
Import the booking link and build out the entire website
questions.explain: Front Desk setup is connect platform ‚Üí set up Zoca's number ‚Üí pick voice ‚Üí set call forwarding ‚Üí live test call. The test call is the trust moment.

questions.q: An owner asks 'why am I putting my card down if I'm not getting charged?' What's the cleanest reframe?
options: Because billing is actually handled by Netflix as the processor
Because Zoca streams the entire training video library on demand for free
Because the trial includes free streaming movies during onboarding
Like Netflix ‚Äî card on file, free week, cancel any time
questions.explain: The Netflix framing lands fast: card on file starts a free week, no charge until day 7, cancel any time during the trial. Familiar pattern, low resistance.

questions.q: Day 9, a customer's card payment fails. What happens?
options: Access is cut off instantly with no warning given
The 7-day trial restarts from day one automatically
A backup card on file is auto-charged silently
Short grace period to resolve it before access closes
questions.explain: A failed charge triggers a short grace period to fix the card before access closes ‚Äî not instant lockout, not trial restart.

questions.q: A franchise group with 8 locations across 2 states wants to onboard today. What's the right move?
options: Onboarding today is built for single-location shops; 5+ escalates
Onboard all 8 locations together in one session
Refuse ‚Äî multi-location franchises aren't supported at all
Tell them to onboard one location, figure out rest later
questions.explain: Onboarding flow today is built for solo and single-location shops. 5+ locations is enterprise territory ‚Äî escalate rather than trying to close it solo.

questions.q: Why does the team insist on confirming the current environment before any live setup?
options: Pricing differs by environment, so it has to be confirmed first
Production is always the most up-to-date environment of all
The prospect picks the environment they want to onboard in
The newest build ships to demo/sandbox first; production lags
questions.explain: The newest features ship to demo/sandbox first; production trails by days or weeks. Confirming the environment avoids onboarding a customer into a stale build.

questions.q: A prospect asks where her card details actually sit. What's the honest answer?
options: Directly on Zoca's own servers in encrypted form
On the salon's current booking platform's account vault
Only on the owner's local device in iOS keychain
With Zoca's billing provider, not Zoca directly
questions.explain: Card data lives with Zoca's billing provider (the payment processor), not on Zoca's servers ‚Äî standard PCI-safe pattern that owners are familiar with from any SaaS.

questions.q: A 3-month customer wants to add Loyalty Agent. What's the contract impact?
options: She signs a brand-new contract for the new agent
Existing contract augments automatically ‚Äî same card, no re-signing
Her 7-day trial restarts from day one on add
She must book an offboarding call before adding agents
questions.explain: One contract per business. Adding agents later augments it automatically ‚Äî joins the same subscription, same cycle, same card on file, no re-signing.

questions.q: A prospect asks 'what's the single thing I absolutely need in the shop to onboard today?' The honest answer is:
options: Laptop or iPad in the shop ‚Äî the only rule
An iPad mounted permanently at the front desk on a stand
A POS system already running fully on Stripe payments
An existing booking platform on the supported integrations list
questions.explain: A laptop or iPad in the shop is the only genuine hard prerequisite anywhere in onboarding. Everything else flexes.

questions.q: A new rep is practicing the one-line pitch. Which version is the load-bearing one to lead with?
options: An AI agency for small local businesses everywhere
The marketing + voice platform for hyperlocal beauty and wellness
The future of beauty SaaS and modern salon technology stacks today
A voice tool with bolt-on SEO and marketing features
questions.explain: Every word is load-bearing: marketing + voice (both halves), platform (not 'tool' or 'agency'), hyperlocal (the geography), beauty and wellness (the vertical).

questions.q: On a discovery call the owner mentions she has no laptop or iPad anywhere in the shop. What's the right move?
options: Tell her she doesn't qualify for Zoca and end the call
Onboard her over the phone instead of the screen-share
Refer her to a competitor who can run setup remotely
Get a laptop or iPad to the front desk first
questions.explain: Laptop/iPad in the shop is the ONLY true hard rule in the whole curriculum ‚Äî onboarding can't run without it. The move is to get the device there, not turn the prospect away.

questions.q: A solo operator at $40K/yr, one location, no staff wants in. How do you classify her?
options: Outside the vertical entirely ‚Äî refer her to another vendor
Disqualified from buying ‚Äî she falls under the revenue floor
Best-fit, move fast ‚Äî exactly Zoca's ideal customer profile
Lower-fit, not a no ‚Äî sellable with honest expectations
questions.explain: ICP is best-fit, not a wall. A sub-$100K solo shop is lower-fit ‚Äî sellable with honest expectation-setting about smaller, slower wins. Never refused.

questions.q: A prospect cites $249/month from an old product doc she found online. What's the right rep response?
options: Honor the $249 since she has documented proof of it
Treat the $249 from the doc as the official current price
Quote her $290 instead to anchor the conversation higher
Reject as stale, quote the placeholder ‚Äî pricing pending RevOps
questions.explain: $179 / $249 / $269 / $279 / $290 are ALL stale. Pricing is pending final confirmation ‚Äî reject stale numbers on sight and use the placeholder of record.

questions.q: An owner asks 'so are you guys an AI agency or a software company?' The right answer is:
options: An AI agency ‚Äî we build custom marketing strategy decks for the owners
A platform ‚Äî marketing + voice for hyperlocal beauty, not an agency
Both ‚Äî we sell both an agency service and software
Neither ‚Äî we're closer to a daily-deal platform like Groupon
questions.explain: We are a platform, not an agency. 'Agency' connotes a strategy deck and a human running 12 accounts ‚Äî the wrong frame for productized, at-scale execution.

questions.q: A salon owner says 'I get 30 calls a day, my staff just can't pick them all up.' Which leak is this, and which agent closes it?
options: Missed calls ‚Äî Front Desk Agent (Zoe)
First-timer churn ‚Äî the Loyalty Agent
Visibility gap ‚Äî the Discovery Agent
Mid-booking drop-off ‚Äî the Conversion Agent handles this
questions.explain: Missed calls is the ~22% leak. Front Desk Agent (Zoe) picks up 24/7 in under a second and books on the call ‚Äî the literal answer to 'my staff can't pick them all up.'

questions.q: Of the four leaks, which is the single most leveraged because the customer already chose the business?
options: New bookings / visibility gap
Missed inbound calls during business hours
Mid-booking drop-off (the Black Box)
First-timer churn after the first appointment
questions.explain: Mid-booking drop-off (the Black Box) is most leveraged ‚Äî the intent already happened. The customer found the salon and started booking; they just didn't finish.

questions.q: Which four percentages are the leak-benchmark numbers a rep should have memorized?
options: 22% / 31% / 37% / 41% across the four leaks identified by Zoca
37 visibility / 22 missed calls / 31 mid-booking / 52 first-timer
31% / 48% / 52% / 70% across the four
3% / 22% / 41% / 52% across the four
questions.explain: The spine of every discovery call: 37 (visibility), 22 (missed calls), 31 (mid-booking drop), 52 (first-timer churn). Know them cold.

questions.q: An owner says 'I don't have a marketing problem.' What's the reframe?
options: Tell her she's flat wrong about marketing not being her issue
Confirm she's not a fit for Zoca and politely close the call
She has a capture problem, not a demand problem
She has a demand problem you need to fix before anything else
questions.explain: Owners almost never have a demand problem ‚Äî demand exists. They have a capture problem: not enough time, staff, or tools to convert the demand that's already searching for them.

questions.q: An owner says 'I already pay an agency $1,500/mo and they handle this.' What's the right move?
options: Bash the agency on the call to win the deal away
Refuse to discuss the agency and steer to pricing
Promise to beat the agency's price with a custom discount
Reframe ‚Äî agencies can't compete on execution at scale
questions.explain: Never bash the incumbent ‚Äî the owner chose them. Reframe: agencies are great at strategy decks; we compete on execution at scale (continuous output for one customer, not 12).

questions.q: A new AE thinks ICP means a hard gate that filters out under-qualified prospects. What's the actual definition?
options: A hard revenue floor every prospect must clear first
A hard gate filtering out anyone below the bar
A list of businesses Zoca explicitly refuses to ever serve as customers
A best-fit targeting and expectation-setting tool, not a gate
questions.explain: ICP at Zoca is best-fit framing ‚Äî targeting + expectation-setting. It tells you who pays off fastest, not who you refuse. Turning away paying customers is explicitly wrong.

questions.q: A tattoo studio reaches out. Where do tattoo, piercing, and permanent makeup studios fall?
options: Outside the vertical entirely ‚Äî refuse them politely
Low-ticket excluded categories under Zoca's hard floor today
In-vertical beauty ‚Äî sold like any beauty shop
Verify with Sales Ops before quoting any pricing
questions.explain: Tattoo, piercing, and PMU are in-vertical beauty categories ‚Äî they sell like any other beauty shop. Don't second-guess and don't escalate; close them.

questions.q: What's the decided lead-prediction signal for a best-fit shop?
options: At least 60 new leads in the next six months
At least 100 new leads per month every single month consistently
Pending Sales Ops review of the final number
At least $100K in annual top-line revenue today
questions.explain: ~60 new leads in 6 months is the decided signal ‚Äî not pending Sales Ops, not monthly. Below that, deals still close but the wins are smaller and slower.

questions.q: A dentist with real budget wants to buy Zoca. The right approach is:
options: Decline because they're outside the beauty and wellness vertical
Sell as if the product is fully tuned for dental customers
Tell them they don't qualify and refer them to a competitor
Be honest the product's tuned for beauty, let them decide
questions.explain: Beauty & wellness is the sharpest fit but never a wall. Out-of-vertical owners are still sellable ‚Äî be honest about the trade-offs and let them choose.

questions.q: A franchise owner with 12 locations across 3 states calls in. How does this fall in our ICP framework, and what's the next step?
options: 5+ locations is enterprise ‚Äî escalate, don't quote solo
Best-fit ‚Äî quote standard per-location pricing and close today
Solo lower-fit ‚Äî close monthly without escalating to a manager
Refuse the deal ‚Äî franchise networks aren't supported at all
questions.explain: 2-4 locations = per-location at base rate. 5+ locations = enterprise territory; escalate to the enterprise lead. Don't quote the standard multi-loc number ‚Äî it doesn't scale to franchise networks.

questions.q: A prospect asks 'so what am I actually buying?' What's Discovery Neo, in one line?
options: Discovery + Front Desk Agents bundled ‚Äî can't be split
All five agents on five separate active subscriptions
Only the Front Desk Agent with calling and booking
A booking platform with a built-in AI receptionist plugin and dashboard
questions.explain: Discovery Neo = Discovery Agent (marketing brain) + Front Desk Agent (voice brain), bundled as ONE product. Every new logo gets both; they cannot be unbundled.

questions.q: Of the three operating modes (Approve / Supervised / Auto), which is the default and what does it mean?
options: Supervised ‚Äî agent acts; Content Queue surfaces big decisions
Approve ‚Äî every action gated until the owner taps approve
Auto ‚Äî full autopilot with no human review at all
Manual ‚Äî the owner does every action themselves end-to-end

questions.q: An owner asks for the prices of the Loyalty and Conversion add-ons. The correct answer is:

Both bundled into the base plan at no extra cost ever
Loyalty $49/mo (500 SMS + 100 calls); Conversion $49/mo + 10%

questions.q: A prospect asks 'who do you use for the voice AI under the hood?' What's the right answer?
options: It's all built in house ‚Äî we don't name vendors
Name the third-party voice vendor that powers the Front Desk Agent today
We license the voice stack from a partner under NDA
We can't discuss the voice infrastructure at all here

questions.q: A spa owner asks 'does Zoe take a deposit on the call?' What's the honest answer?
options: Yes ‚Äî she charges the card live during the actual call
Yes, but only when Zoca Scheduling is the active platform
No ‚Äî Zoe orchestrates, doesn't charge live on the call
She emails the customer a Stripe payment link after the call
questions.explain: Taking deposits/cards live on the call is out of scope today. Zoe orchestrates (triggers the platform's deposit flow) ‚Äî she does not process the payment on the call. Don't promise no-show protection by charging on-call.

questions.q: What's the most common alternative an owner is actually weighing against Zoca?
options: A marketing or SEO agency on retainer
A deal platform like Groupon for promotions
A legacy booking platform with an AI plugin
Doing nothing and living with the leak
questions.explain: Doing nothing ‚Äî living with the leak ‚Äî is the most common alternative. Selling against Zoca means selling against inertia first, competitors second.

questions.q: An owner says 'Zoca leads are just Groupon leads.' What's the core reframe rooted in?
options: Search intent ‚Äî branded vs. non-branded search behavior
Zoca offering a bigger discount than Groupon does
Groupon's higher platform fees per booked appointment
Zoca also being listed on Groupon as a partner
questions.explain: Search intent decides everything. Groupon customers searched a branded promotion ('Groupon facial deal'); Zoca leads searched non-branded service terms ('facial near me') and pay full price. Different buyer entirely.

questions.q: An owner says 'We already pay GlossGenius ‚Äî they have an AI thing now.' The best move is:
options: Tell her to rip out GlossGenius and switch over entirely
Ask if GlossGenius is doing SEO/content; clarify we connect
Bash GlossGenius as a legacy tool with bolted-on AI
Concede she's already covered and politely end the call
questions.explain: The existing-vendor objection is usually partial coverage masquerading as full. Find the gap (SEO, content, AI search, outbound) and clarify Zoca connects, doesn't replace, the booking system.

questions.q: What's Zoca's moat per the lesson?
options: Lowest price in the local marketing software market today
The largest dedicated sales team in beauty tech currently
Vertical depth ‚Äî built only for beauty and wellness
Owning the customer relationship like a daily-deal platform
questions.explain: Vertical depth is the moat. A horizontal platform can't build the category intelligence, service vocabulary, and rebook patterns Zoca builds because we only build for beauty and wellness.

questions.q: An owner says 'I'm running Booksy plus a voice-AI plugin already.' What's the unifying reframe?
options: Promise to beat their combined monthly price with a flat custom discount today
Tell them to rip out Booksy and move entirely onto Zoca
Concede the plugin covers it and back off the deal politely
One brain beats a bolt-on ‚Äî shared context across phone, web, chat
questions.explain: The unifying win across competing setups: 'one brain beats a bolt-on.' Shared context layer across Discovery + Front Desk is what no booking-plus-plugin stack can stitch together cleanly.

questions.q: A rep is writing website copy and is about to use 'no contracts.' What should it say instead, and why?
options: 'No contracts' is fine because the trial is fully cancellable
'No long-term contracts' ‚Äî service agreements are signed at trial start
'Zero-commitment' since the customer can leave at any time during the trial
'Cancel anytime, no agreement required to start your trial'
questions.explain: Public-facing copy is 'no long-term contracts.' Annual is a 1-year service agreement; monthly is 30-day notice. 'No contracts' is inaccurate and breaks Value 04 (honesty).

questions.q: Looking at the April 2026 SDR incident (34 sales SMS reached paid customers), what was the root failure?

questions.explain: The exclusion filter was applied at list-prep rather than send time ‚Äî paid customers slipped in. The copy also carried performance-shaming language. Two failures, both honesty-rooted.

questions.q: When running the six-value filter on a tough decision no policy covers, which two questions catch most bad calls?
options: #1 (does this serve the customer?) and #2 (am I honest?)
#5 (dreaming big) and #6 (betting on yourself first)
#3 (figure it out) and #4 (boring vs the bold move call)
#4 (the bold move) and #5 (betting on the people)
questions.explain: Most bad decisions fail at value #1 (customer winning) or #2 (honesty). If a choice passes both, the rest usually resolves; if it fails either, don't do it.

questions.q: On a discovery call, how should an AE describe Booking, Loyalty, and Ads Agents?
options: As live features included in the base bundle today
As Coming Soon upside, sold without a launch date
As features shipping next week if the prospect signs today
As permanently unavailable, not even worth mentioning live

questions.q: A prospect asks for a 20% discount because she's 'a friend of a friend.' What does Value 04 (honesty) point you to?
options: Match the 20% discount on the spot to be helpful
Quote her the stale $249 price to make her feel special
Escalate to a manager for one-off discount approval today
Hold price ‚Äî no AE discount floor; annual IS the discount
questions.explain: No discounts beyond annual. The annual rate is the discount, full stop. Discounting feels generous but trains the prospect that price is soft and creates renewal pain.

questions.q: As of May 2026, which booking platforms are the confirmed LIVE Zoca integrations a rep can promise today?
options: Booksy and Vagaro
Square and Mindbody
GlossGenius and Fresha
Boulevard and Acuity
questions.explain: Only GlossGenius and Fresha are confirmed integrated today. Booksy, Vagaro, Square, Mindbody are roadmap. Boulevard, Acuity, StyleSeat, Calendly, Schedulicity are NOT supported.

questions.q: A salon on Boulevard asks if Zoca integrates. What's the honest answer?
options: Boulevard's not supported ‚Äî scope a migration or be upfront
Yes ‚Äî Boulevard is fully supported as a live integration today
Yes ‚Äî Boulevard support is shipping by end of this quarter
Yes ‚Äî we can build a custom Boulevard integration this week
questions.explain: Boulevard is not a supported calendar ‚Äî never promise it. The right move is honesty: scope a migration to a live platform (GlossGenius/Fresha) or be upfront and let them decide.

questions.q: An owner asks 'does Zoca process my payments directly?' What's the right answer?
options: Zoca processes all customer payments through its own payment rail
Zoca replaces the booking platform's payment system entirely on day one
Zoca routes payments through a generic third-party CRM-based system
Zoca orchestrates ‚Äî triggers the platform's payment flow, never processes
questions.explain: Orchestrate, don't process. Front Desk Agent calls back into the booking platform's payment flow (Booksy, Vagaro, Square) ‚Äî Zoca never processes payments on its own rail.

questions.q: A prospect's booking platform is on the roadmap but not live yet. What's the move?
options: Tell them the deal is dead and politely move on now
Treat as a migration ‚Äî scope setup honestly, let them decide
Promise the integration ships next week if they sign now
Refuse to engage unless they switch platforms immediately today
questions.explain: A not-yet-live platform is never a hard no. It becomes a migration conversation: scope the setup honestly (e.g., move to GlossGenius/Fresha) and let the owner decide.

questions.q: A prospect on Calendly asks about Zoca. What's the right answer?
options: Yes, Calendly is fully supported as a live integration today
Yes, Calendly works through a Zapier workaround we built
Calendly isn't supported ‚Äî scope a migration or be upfront
Yes, Calendly support is shipping next month with the next release
questions.explain: Calendly, Acuity, StyleSeat, Schedulicity, and Boulevard are not supported and shouldn't be promised. Scope a migration or be upfront ‚Äî never bluff support.

questions.q: Why does the qualifying call save the revenue question for later instead of leading with it?
options: Revenue is mostly irrelevant to figuring out customer fit
Owners get defensive; location/staff already reveal size by then
Reps aren't allowed to ask revenue at all on a first call
Revenue has to be the very last question of the call always
questions.explain: Leading with revenue makes owners defensive. Location and staff questions reveal size early; by the time you ask revenue, it feels like normal scoping, not interrogation.

questions.q: What's the decided lead-prediction signal for healthy demand?
options: At least 60 leads over the next six months
At least 100 leads per month for every month
At least 60 leads per month every single month
Pending Sales Ops decision on the final lead number this quarter
questions.explain: 60 leads in 6 months ‚Äî settled, not pending. Below that, deals still close; the wins are just smaller and slower.

questions.q: A solo single-location shop owner doing under $100K is on the call. How does the AE handle fit?
options: Disqualify ‚Äî she doesn't meet the revenue floor for Zoca
Refuse and tell her to come back at $500K in revenue
Quote a discounted price below the floor to win her today
Workable lower-fit ‚Äî sellable with honest, modest expectations
questions.explain: Fit is best-fit, not a hard no. Sub-$100K solo shop is workable lower-fit ‚Äî set honest expectations about smaller, slower wins and let her decide. Never refuse and never discount.

questions.q: A prospect asks about Conversion Agent pricing during qualification. Which statement is correct?
options: Loyalty is free; Conversion has no platform prerequisite required
Ads Agent is $49/mo flat with no transaction or platform fee
Conversion is $49/mo + 10%, requires B&P connected
Bookings & Payments costs $49/mo flat with no transaction fee

questions.q: An owner mentions she's been in business 3 months. How does this shape the qualifying call?
options: Disqualify ‚Äî she's far too new for any meaningful results yet
Flag it ‚Äî push monthly, set honest expectations, revisit later
Quote her the annual price with no setup-fee waiver applied
Promise her aggressive growth numbers to lock the deal in
questions.explain: Brand-new businesses (<6 months) often have unclear intent and demand. Push monthly (the off-ramp), set honest expectations, and revisit. Don't oversell or refuse.

questions.q: What's the purpose of the Day 0 to Wk 3 toggle reveal in the demo?
options: To show a hidden discount tier inside the dashboard preview area today
To set honest expectations ‚Äî Day 0 to Wk 3 reveal
To demonstrate the billing cycle exactly as shown in dashboard interface
To compare Zoca's dashboard against an agency's monthly report
questions.explain: Day 0 ‚Üí Wk 3 reveal is the single most powerful demo move. It pre-empts churn by setting an honest expectation: the dashboard starts empty and fills as the agents work.

questions.q: During the live Test Call, a prospect asks 'wait, is this actually AI?' How should the AE answer?
options: Name the third-party voice vendor that powers the Front Desk Agent
Deny it's actually AI to keep some of the magic intact
Refuse to answer the question and move on to the next section
It's the Front Desk Agent, built in-house ‚Äî never name vendors
questions.explain: Honest: it's the Front Desk Agent, built in-house. Never name a third-party voice vendor on a customer call. Honesty about it being AI builds trust.

questions.q: At roughly what point in the canonical 20-minute demo should pricing be revealed?
options: Before any screen-sharing begins, at the very start of demo
Minute 4 ‚Äî right after the opening introduction wraps
Minute 12, during the four promises section of demo
Near the end (minute 17-18) after gap and fixes
questions.explain: Pricing reveal is held to minute 18 by design. The prospect needs to have felt the gap (audit) and seen the fixes (Test Call) before the number lands.

questions.q: An owner asks 'can your AI book group bookings for bachelorette parties on the call?' How should you handle this?
